# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

Category Core · Layer Feature · Priority MVP · Effort M. Specialists: engine-programmer (primary), technical-director, gameplay-programmer.

Anti-pillars honoured by omission: no combat (nothing in Body can displace another actor), no PvP, no freeform builder (`heading_q` locked 0, weld legality takes no pose input), no authored story, no win state.
11	> **Design Review (first formal review, 2026-10-27)**: 2 BLOCKING items applied (AC-BDY-74 split into an automated gate and a playtest on the shipped build; the cap-trap exposure rule stated honestly in BDY-16, BDY-29 and D.11) and the RECOMMENDED items that needed no new creative direction; declined and open items are in Open Questions 30 to 40 (the declined 2^21 `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` default is row 35). Every edited paragraph or row is marked *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
12	> **Design Re-Review (2026-10-27)**: 2 BLOCKING items applied (the mutator contract rewritten so every mutator returns OK or a FAULT_CODE, check-then-write, with an explicit per-defect-class split and an injectable `plan_mismatch_sink`; the weld and cut camera behaviour restated as the Pipeline's C5 REBASE with `frame_delta_px` defined) and the RECOMMENDED items that needed no new creative direction (D.14 gating, the `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` counting rule, a recompute-on-read `trapped_actors()`, the restore contract, 64-bit columns, the D.12 cost model, the test plan and evidence). 13	> **Cross-GDD fix pass (2026-10-28)**: seat-binding rebuild answered by the kernel (BDY-7, KRN-BIND-01; AC-BDY-6 and 138 become Body's epic closure gate); canonical bytes are the kernel's D.12 TLV of a five-key payload, the hand-written s32/s64 writer and the 208-byte golden are deleted (BDY-32 (3), D.9, AC-BDY-110, golden now 518 bytes); the hatch-cap entombment guard is ruled REFUSE with BM4's fifth argument `cap_rects[]` and `BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP` (BDY-24 (iii), AC-BDY-140 and 141); reference machines RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK close Open Question 37 (R12, D.12); Open Questions 1 to 4 are resolved (R21); the Interaction consumer edge is recorded (4.2). Every edited paragraph or row is marked *(Amended 2026-10-28 — ...)*.
14	> **Creative Director Review (CD-GDD-ALIGN)**: CONCERNS → REVISED 2026-10-26 (1 items applied; skipped: Item 4 (Player Fantasy MDA Discovery sentence): already present in the 'The emotion named: footing' paragraph, citing anti-pillar guard rail (6); verified and left unchanged, logged as such.)
15	
16	## Summary
17	
18	Ship Body & Interior Physics decides where every crew member is standing on the ship's deck and how a ship that moves through the void can be joined to another or cut in two without the floor ever moving under anyone's feet. It keeps each person's position as a whole-pixel number in the ship's own frame, stops them exactly at the wall footprints the level data gives it, and re-expresses those positions by plain arithmetic when Assembly welds a wreck on, cuts a section off, or the pod hops across. The player never sees it as a mechanic; they feel it as footing, a deck that stays put no matter what the web does outside.
19	
20	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer` (designed), `Ship Section & Layout Data Model` (designed), `Player Controller & Input` (designed), `Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera` (designed); downstream, `Modular Ship Assembly` and `Web Map & Transit` are now designed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: was "undesigned (provisional)")*
21	
22	## Overview
23	
24	**The framing conflict, stated first.** The systems index describes this system as "the composite ship as one physics body with a ship-local reference frame; characters and props moving inside a moving body (the moving-platform problem); detach spawns a new body" (IDX:29). Read as a mandate to build an engine physics body per ship, that sentence is wrong for this game, and four designed GDDs have already removed engine physics from it: the Controller says "the avatar has no physics body" and moves it by a hand-rolled integer `LocomotionStep` (PCI:103, PC-14 PCI:143); Layout's rectangles are simulation data "never produced by an engine physics shape" and its projector builds no engine tile collision and no navigation mesh in the MVP (LY-7, LY-31); the Emitter's occlusion is an integer segment-versus-rectangle test and "physics-derived observations never enter this block" (EM-30); and the Pipeline draws the interior in the avatar's body frame at the canvas origin, where "ship motion through the void never appears in the interior view" and "ship rotation is never rendered inside" (PIPE C2). The consequence, which this GDD adopts as its first rule (BDY-2, BDY-3): **in the MVP the moving-platform problem is a data problem, not an engine problem.** Every actor's position is an integer in its body's own frame; the composite welded ship is ONE body because Layout holds exactly one `body_id` per welded set (LY-18); a body that moves through the exterior therefore cannot move anything standing inside it, and a weld, a cut or a pod hop is integer arithmetic on stored positions. *(orchestrator ruling R1: option (a), an integer kinematic frame with a pose-invariant interior; options (b) one engine rigid body per ship and (c) an engine-physics exterior hybrid are rejected, the second surviving only as the presentation-only ADR-BODY-05 candidate.)*
25	
26	**What it is, in one sentence.** Ship Body & Interior Physics is the single owner of *where each actor is inside its body* and *how each body sits in the exterior frame*: a scene-tree-free, integer-only `SIM` block (`body.state`) that holds every actor's body-frame kinematic state and every body's sparse pose and velocity, one per-tick hook (`body.integrate`) that runs the pure `LocomotionStep` sweep against Layout's rectangles, seven mutators that re-home actors when Assembly welds, cuts or Transit hops a pod, or set a body's exterior velocity or pose, a handful of pure reads, and one `PROJECTOR` subscriber that owns the per-body scene root and the camera-limit rectangle. Layout owns the geometry and the `body_id`; the Controller owns intent, octant, gait and the chest point; the Pipeline owns frame composition; Assembly and Transit own the commands that move actors between bodies. Body owns the one thing none of them do: the integer position of a person on a deck, and the arithmetic that keeps it true when the deck is joined to another or cut in two.
27	
28	**Who owns what (closes the kernel's and the Controller's open boundary).** *Ship Body owns ship-local integer position* — `pos_curr`, `sub`, `last_octant`, `odometer`, `blocked`, the foot box, the sweep, the body transfers and the `LocomotionStep` — *and the Controller owns intent, octant, gait, `v_eff`, committed aim, facing, locomotion state, carry and channel references, the chest point and the hand point.* This closes kernel Open Question 3 (KRN:194, KRN:958) and the Controller's PC-14 recommendation (PCI:143, PCI:1108), which both asked for exactly this split. Body reads `octant` and `v_eff` from `controller.state` and derives nothing of the Controller's (BDY-11). The lamp is **chest**-mounted and hands-free (user decision): if this GDD names a beam origin at all it is the chest point, which the Controller publishes; the foot origin Body owns is the shadow and occluder origin (LO-10); the hand point is a lightless tool grip and nothing in Body touches it.
29	
30	**How the player meets it.** Never as a menu, a gauge, a velocity readout or a mechanic. The player meets Body as *footing*: a deck that stops exactly where the 24-px wall footprint says it stops (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`), a stop that is pixel-exact with no overshoot, a wall that is slid along rather than stuck to, and — at the two moments the game is most violent on paper — a weld and a cut during which nothing at all happens to the floor under their boots. Ship motion, docking contact and hull separation are events out in the exterior layer and the sound of the hull; they are never forces on the interior (BDY-28). The only things the player *does* that reach Body are walking and the Assembly and Transit verbs that Body's mutators serve, and each lands in `body.state` as an atomic, replayable change.
31	
32	**What the game loses without it.** Nothing else owns the integer position of a person on a deck. Without Body, `LocomotionStep` has no home and the Controller's 12 sweep tests (PC-18) have no module; Suit's room lookup (SE-3) has no `section_id` to supply; the Emitter's ACTOR anchor (EM-21) and the lamp's shadow origin (LO-10) have no `pos_curr` to read, and `emitter.state`'s `restore_after: [layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]` (EM-1) names a block that does not exist, which fails boot; Save/Load's mandatory set (SL:288) has no `body.state` and the kernel's restore-idempotence debt (`REBASE_BLOCKS`, SL:577) stays open; a weld or cut would leave every actor standing in a frame that no longer exists; and the weld spike — the riskiest MVP task, the reason this system was added to the index as a `TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY` addition (IDX:65, IDX:276) — would have no owner for "the motion". Because the spike is *weld on a moving ship*, the GDD's answer is that welding is safe by construction: weld legality takes no pose input (BDY-27), and the interior never reads the pose.
33	
34	**Scope guard: what Body does not own.** Geometry, `body_id` allocation, membership, offsets, welds, sockets, seams, hatch states and door leaves are Layout's (LY-18, LY-35); Body owns *pose and actors only*. **No prop is a Body actor in the MVP** (BDY-4): loose items are Interaction records in section-local pixels, so "a weld or a detach moves nothing" (IA-28, LY-22); static props and machinery are Layout rectangles; a thrown glowstick lands by an analytic rule (IA-29); a horror's footprint is a Graph trail, never a Body fact. The index's word "props" is therefore satisfied by a statement, not a mechanism; a Vertical Slice movable prop adds one `kind` here and one bump-list entry in Layout deliberately (LY:229). Intent, gait and the chest point belong to the Controller; camera, zoom, the cut rule and the exterior/transit layers to the Pipeline; weld and cut commands, weld quality `q` and the order of mutators to Assembly and the Graph; the loaded set, the pod leg and the docking script to Web Map & Transit; atmosphere and damage to the Life-Support Graph; sanity and perceived values to Sanity and the Perception Filter. There is no HUD element, no overlay and no number that the player reads from Body. **MVP slice.** In: SEAT actors only (one seat, `MAX_ACTORS` 8); `LocomotionStep` and the sweep; BM1–BM7; weld (BM3) and cut (BM4) on the home-ship 5 / derelict A 4 / derelict B 5 compartment slice; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, X1: the weld, the player seam cut and the install are all MVP, so BM3 and BM4 serving a player-initiated cut carry no cut-first status; co-op stays out of the MVP)* the pod hop (BM5) and a constant-velocity pod leg (BM6); restore idempotence; `body.projector` with rotation 0. Later (Vertical Slice): AGENT rows for horrors (if Horror picks that path), `DETACH_DRIFT_PX_PER_TICK` > 0, sub-pixel exterior velocity, cross-body light, co-op replication (VS-B), presentation-only debris (ADR-BODY-05), actor soft separation.
35	
36	**Noun guard.** In concept prose "a body they assembled" means the composite ship. In this GDD **`body` / `body_id` is the rigid frame of a welded set** — Layout's id (LY-18), the thing that has a pose — and **"the avatar" or "an actor" is the person standing in it**. Internal nouns (`body`, `body_id`, `pos_curr`, frame, pose, velocity, transfer) are correct in rules and formulas and are never what the player experiences (see Player Fantasy, Language). The word "body" never becomes flesh: flesh tones and violet are reserved for sanity leaks (P1 sane palette), so no Body-originated cue may use them.
37	
38	**Engine statement (which 2D physics path this relies on).** *None.* The only 2D physics server in Godot 4.7.2 is Godot Physics 2D — **verified-from-docs**: `docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/physics.md` (4.6 changes) records "2D physics UNCHANGED (still Godot Physics 2D)", and `VERSION.md` shows Jolt as the 3D default since 4.6, which does not apply to 2D. Body uses that server for nothing on any simulation-authoritative path (BDY-3). The single candidate use is presentation-only debris at Vertical Slice (ADR-BODY-05), excluded from the simulation hash set (`ALL_SIM`). Because nothing is sampled from a physics step, the kernel's determinism limit G3 ("Godot Physics 2D makes no determinism claim, so G3 either records and replays [physics results] or excludes physics-coupled blocks", KRN:123, CR-13) is met by construction: `body.state` is a pure function of the command stream and Layout, kernel Open Question 5 is moot for the MVP, and the kernel row "hook sampling physics results into its block each tick" (KRN:198) collapses to `body.integrate` with nothing sampled (wording note routed in Cross-References). Everything this GDD says about `_physics_process` ordering, 2D interpolation, `TileMapLayer`, `Node.reparent`, GDScript integer-division semantics and canvas float precision is **[UNV]**: the engine reference has no `scripting.md`, `core.md`, `2d.md` or `tilemap.md` (its `modules/` holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui only), and those claims are routed to the weld and motion spikes. Post-cutoff claims used here are tagged verified-from-docs against `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 packed-array element writes no longer call the property setter; typed-return overrides need an explicit `return` on every path).
39	
40	**Index wording, reconciled.** "The composite ship as one physics body with a ship-local reference frame" = one `body_id` per welded set (Layout) plus one sparse pose row per `body_id` (Body), where the *ship-local frame* is Layout's body frame (LY-3 (b)) and the frame's origin is the point Body locates in the exterior frame. "Characters and props moving inside a moving body (the moving-platform problem)" = BDY-2: positions are body-frame integers and nothing keyed on one reads the pose; props: BDY-4. "Detach spawns a new body" = Layout allocates the new `body_id` and returns `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}` (LY-17); Body creates the pose row from the old body's and re-homes the actors on the new side (BDY-23). "Physics PROJECTOR" (KRN:198) = `body.projector`, which builds nothing physical (BDY-33).
41	
42	*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (→ `/architecture-decision`): the motion model and sweep formulation, hand-rolled integer kinematics against any engine body (ADR-BODY-01); the `body.state` shape, the persisted-versus-derived split and restore idempotence (ADR-BODY-02); the scene projection of a body, reparent-on-weld against rebuild, shared with ADR-LAY-03, and the camera-limit rectangle (ADR-BODY-03); the tick source and interpolation clock, shared with the kernel's tick ADR (ADR-BODY-04); and whether presentation-only debris may use engine physics at Vertical Slice (ADR-BODY-05).*
43

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

123	#### 1.1 Identity, ownership and the no-physics-server rule
124	
125	**BDY-1 — One body per welded set; Body adds pose, not geometry.** A body's identity is Layout's `body_id` (LY-18: Layout allocates it from `next_body_id`, first id 1, and owns `bodies[]`, `section_instances[].body_id`, offsets and `welds[]`). Body stores, per `body_id`, only the frame's POSE (`world_x`, `world_y`), its velocity (`vel_x`, `vel_y`) and the reserved `heading_q`, and, per actor, the actor's body-frame state. Body never allocates, retires or edits a `body_id`, section membership, offset, rectangle, socket, seam or hatch state. The composite welded ship is therefore ONE body in exactly the sense the index means: one frame, one pose row, one rectangle set (`solid_in(body_id, aabb)`), however many sections are welded into it. *Decides:* LY-18, LY-35; P1. (review) grep this GDD for `next_body_id`, `welds[]` and `offset_px` as Body-written fields: zero hits.
126	
127	**BDY-2 — The interior is a pose-invariant integer frame.** Every simulation fact about the interior — a foot box, a `solid_in` rectangle, `pos_curr`, an Emitter anchor, Suit's room lookup, the interior camera pose — is a body-frame integer. **Nothing keyed on a body-frame coordinate reads `world_*` or `vel_*`.** A body that moves in the exterior moves nothing inside it, so the moving-platform problem does not exist as an engine problem; a body in motion and a body at rest produce a byte-identical interior (D.9 states the invariance; the acceptance fixture sets a non-zero `vel` on the avatar's body, runs 600 ticks and compares `canonical_encode(payload["actors"])` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*). Rotation is never a simulation fact (BDY-26). *Decides:* R1, R6, P1, PIPE C2 (PIPE:153). (lint + auto)

142	
143	**BDY-8 — `body.integrate` registration and order.** `hook_id body.integrate`, owner Ship Body, divisor 1, offset 0, **`after: [controller.step, layout.doors]`**. This resolves Layout Open Question 6 and LY-10 (LY:217-218) inside Body's own registration: an opening `area` or `door_state` changes only in P2; `layout.doors` runs in P3 and writes the leaf rectangle set; `body.integrate` reads that set in the same tick. 145	**BDY-9 — Per-tick order inside `body.integrate`; the hook is total.** (i) *Pose.* For each `bodies` row in ascending `body_id`, `world += vel` (BDY-26), before any actor steps. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Immediately before the add the derived, non-persisted `world_prev := world` is set (BDY-26 states its reset rules on every discontinuous write). The earlier reading "(iii) derives `actor_section` per tick" is struck, so BDY-9 and BDY-29 no longer disagree and a tick with no exempt actor pays nothing for sections. **Allocation-free hook (budgeted whole, D.12):** the hook allocates no `Array`, `Dictionary`, `RefCounted` or `Vector2i` per tick: the actors table is held as id-sorted struct-of-arrays, `PackedInt32Array` for the s32 columns and `PackedInt64Array` for the two s64 columns (`actor_id` and `odometer`: a 2^53 + 7 odometer must not truncate, AC-BDY-137), kept sorted by the mutators (insertion by binary search in BM1, deletion in BM2, never a sort at tick time; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* the struct-of-arrays layout is the working assumption, not a contract, and spike S1 records it against an array-of-records form because copy-on-write and lookup cost are unmeasured, Open Question 46; the snapshot shape of BDY-31 is independent of it), `LocomotionStep` writes into a caller-owned scratch record (BDY-10), and the `solid_in` result lands in a caller-owned `PackedInt32Array` (BDY-15). 149	| `actor.body_id` not live in Layout | actor skipped (not stepped, not moved), row kept | `BDY_ORPHAN_ACTOR` |
150	| `octant` not in 0..8 | treated as NONE | `BDY_OCTANT_INVALID` |

(auto: PC-18 tests 1-3)
164	
165	**BDY-14 — Foot box, foot origin, first legal row.** `foot_box(actor) = [pos.x - 8, pos.x + 8) x [pos.y, pos.y + 8)` in body-frame cells, half-open (LY-7 convention), with `FOOT_BOX_W` 16 and `FOOT_BOX_H` 8 (Body-registered, confirming PCI:103). **The foot origin is the box's top-centre**: horizontally centred, and the origin row is the box's top row. `y_foot` is the Pipeline's floored presentation foot row `p.y` (PIPE D.9, `p = floor(prev + (curr - prev) * tick_alpha)`, PIPE:535); the foot origin is the box's top row, so at rest (`pos_prev == pos_curr`: a stop, `post_restore`, a transfer) `y_foot = pos_curr.y` and the first-legal-row corollary (`y_0 + 24`) is literal. That corollary makes both designed examples literal: a body walking north into a wall whose footprint rows are `[y_0, y_0 + 24)` rests with `pos.y = y_foot = y_0 + 24`, "the first legal row south of the wall" (PIPE:543, PIPE:727, PCI:909 "the foot box's top edge rests at 124"); a body walking south into the same wall rests with `pos.y = y_0 - 8` (box bottom flush). A committed `pos` that places a foot-box cell inside a SOLID rectangle is a collision defect (`diag.actor_in_footprint`, `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP`) unless BDY-16 applies. `foot_box` is registered as a formula (D.2), not as two loose constants. Layout's passage extents (16 across an east-west doorway, 8 across a north-south one, LY D.5) are unchanged. **CONFLICT (a moved anchor, swept now rather than later):** every designed line that says the foot origin is the box CENTRE must read "horizontally centred; the foot origin is the box's top row": PCI:103 ("foot-centred"), PCI:447 ("`body.state.pos`, foot-box centre"), PCI:651 ("foot origin (foot-box centre)") and PCI:908 ("foot-centred"); PCI:1001 says only "foot origin" and needs no edit; the other "foot origin" hits in Layout, Emitter, Lighting, Interaction and the Controller name the origin, not the centre, and stand. The origin is 4 px north of the old centre reading; Edge Cases states the consequence for the detach side rule once. *(orchestrator ruling R5: the Stage-1 brief's `y_foot := pos.y - 4` is overruled — it rewrites the Pipeline's PIPE D.12 variable table inside a consumer GDD and needs an art offset the Presenter does not have; top-centre sits inside the authority LY-11 and PCI:1087 already grant Body.)* *Decides:* R5; PIPE D.12; LY-11. (auto: D.2 and D.3 fixtures; spike: both rest poses captured at zoom steps 1 and `k_auto + 2` for art sign-off, because top-centre puts the sprite's contact row on the box's north edge)
166	
167	**BDY-15 — Collision is `solid_in`, exactly, with no margin.** `collide` is Layout's `solid_in(body_id, aabb)` (body frame, key order `(section_id, idx)`, `SOLID` filter, LY-12 (c)), called ONCE per moving actor per tick with the swept bounding box of the whole move — the Minkowski cover of the box over the x-then-y path, at most 19 x 11 cells at `|step| = 3` (`16 + |step_x|` by `8 + |step_y|`, D.12) — and the sweep tests only the returned set; a rectangle not returned cannot be hit by construction. The sweep is 1-px sub-steps, x axis then y axis: before each pixel the destination box is tested against every candidate rectangle and the first refusal stops that axis for the tick. Any faster formulation (an analytic clamp against each rectangle's near edge) is permitted if and only if it is result-identical on every input; an equivalence property test carries the proof (the choice is → ADR-BODY-01). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Baseline and oracle, decided.** The **analytic clamp is the shipped baseline** (Layout already assumes it: "Callers issue ONE `solid_in` per actor per tick with the swept bounding box and sweep analytically against the result", LY-12 (c)); the **literal 1-px stepper above is the specification and the TEST ORACLE only** and is never the production path. The cost model of D.12 prices the clamp, not the stepper. **Allocation-free query:** Body calls `solid_in_into(body_id, aabb, out: PackedInt32Array) -> int` (fills a caller-owned buffer with rectangle indices in key order and returns the count) rather than `solid_in(...)`, which returns a fresh array each call; `solid_in_into` is an additive ASK to Layout (8.3, Open Question 32), and until it exists Body calls `solid_in` and the hot-path allocation criterion (AC-BDY-125) is BLOCKED on it. The buffer is sized once at boot to `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`. There is no inflated margin, no "perceived" variant and no second rectangle set: a wall that blocks the foot but not the eye, or the reverse, is a lie (P1). Collision uses the 24-px footprint, never the 72-px face (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`, art-bible-owned; Layout is not its source). Doors are rectangles Layout has already rewritten (BDY-18). *Decides:* P1, LY-34, T5. (auto: PC-18 tests 5-6; property tests)
168	
169	**BDY-16 — Overlap exemption: the body is never displaced, and an exempt actor can only leave.** Let `E` be the set of SOLID rectangles the actor's foot box intersects **at the start of the actor's tick** (fixed for that tick). Members of `E` arise from a door leaf that closed under the actor, a restore of an older save against a changed template, or a template defect *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* (a cut can no longer cap a hatch under an actor: BM4 refuses it, BDY-24 (iii)). For an actor with a non-empty `E`, a 1-px sub-step on either axis is admitted iff **for every `r` in `E`, `|box_after ∩ r| <= |box_before ∩ r|`** (overlap measured in cells; D.11 states `ov(r)`) **and the destination foot origin lies in a section of the actor's body (exit containment, below)**; every rectangle not in `E` stays fully solid, so an exempt actor cannot walk into a wall it was not already inside. The test is per rectangle, not total: on the `fixture_airlock` hull-line geometry a box astride two abutting exempt rectangles `[672, 696)` and `[696, 720)` keeps its TOTAL overlap at 128 cells while stepping east (one rectangle loses a column, the other gains one), so a total-area test would let it cross the hull line, while the per-rectangle test refuses that step because the east rectangle's own overlap grows; every move along the shared edge (both overlaps unchanged) and every move away (both shrink) stays admitted. `E` is computed afresh each tick from the current box (no stored flag; nothing persisted or hashed). Each exempt actor-tick increments `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` (read 0 in a clean build) and, in debug, fires `diag.actor_in_footprint` (PIPE:727). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What "exempt actor-tick" counts (option (a), adopted).** `E` is computed from a `solid_in` query, and a stationary actor issues none (BDY-9), so the counter increments **once per actor-tick in which `E` was evaluated and found non-empty** (a tick on which the actor requested a non-zero step, so the query ran), **plus once at each detection event whose start-of-tick box test finds `E` non-empty** (placement, a transfer, a weld or cut for every actor on the touched bodies, `post_restore`): a detection event on an actor whose box intersects nothing adds nothing, so a clean weld, cut or restore leaves the counter at 0 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier wording read as an unconditional increment per event)*. An idle exempt actor therefore adds nothing on its idle ticks, and a trapped actor that stops pressing a key stops counting; the counter is a lower bound on exempt time, and its only contract is the QA gate "0 in a clean build" (CI, not a playtest alarm; Tuning Knobs). Stationary overlaps are made visible by the detection events, by the `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR` probe below and by the debug tree-walk (PIPE:727), never by a per-tick query Body does not otherwise issue. A rectangle in `E` is fully solid for the actor again on the first tick whose start box no longer intersects it. **Nothing shoves**: `pos` is unchanged on every tick the actor does not step, and a push-out, shove or snap is struck (an unannounced displacement the player did not cause, P2; it contradicts PCI:650 "the body is never displaced" and LY-11). The rule is strictly tighter than PCI:650's literal "non-solid for that actor until the overlap clears" (PCI:650, PCI:1002); the additive wording row is routed to the Controller in 8.3. Detection happens at placement, at every transfer, at `post_restore` and on every stepping tick; a stationary actor issues no query, so a stationary overlap is caught at those events and by the debug tree-walk. **Exit containment (the second clause of the predicate; P1).** A sub-step that passes the overlap test is ALSO refused if its destination foot ORIGIN (the box top-centre, D.2) lies in no section of the actor's own body (D.10: `actor_section` would answer NONE for that origin). The test reads the sections of the actor's current `body_id` only, so a plate whose section has left the body (the B plate after a cut) is no longer floor for this purpose. The only exits from a hatch cap therefore lead back onto the body's own floor: no exempt sub-step can carry an actor out of the hull, and an exempt step never produces a NONE section. An actor whose START origin is already in no section (a defect, Edge Cases) may step only toward an origin that lies in a section. The reason is that a crew member standing outside the hull while their air, temperature and pressure still came from a room they had left would be a hidden stat contradicting what the world shows, which is the failure the Pillar 1 design test forbids. **What the predicate guarantees, and what it does not.** Any sub-step with a component away from a rectangle in `E` shrinks that rectangle's overlap, so a PARTIALLY overlapping box whose shrinking direction leads onto the body's own floor leaves in a bounded number of ticks and can never deepen. Three residuals are accepted and are defect-only paths: (i) a box wholly inside one rectangle (the common case, because `FOOT_BOX_H` 8 is less than the 24-px strip) has constant overlap until an edge crosses out, so it may exit on either side, including through a closed leaf, provided the destination origin lies in a section of the body (never out of the hull); (ii) a box astride two abutting exempt rectangles can only slide along their shared edge or back out, and if neither reaches open floor it stays exempt in place; (iii) **the cap trap:** an actor in a hatch cap whose only shrinking direction would put its origin outside the body cannot leave. The concrete case: after a restore of a save recorded in that pose against the Layout state holding plate A SOLID, an actor at `pos = (690, 282)` has the box `[682, 698) x [282, 290)` astride the east edge of the cap plate `[672, 696) x [240, 336)` (plate B, `[696, 720)`, belongs to a section that is not part of this body); stepping west deepens the overlap (refused), stepping north or south keeps it (admitted by the overlap test) until the box meets the rectangles that are not in `E` and stay solid (D.11 gives the extent), and stepping east shrinks it and is admitted only while the destination origin is inside plate A: at `V_WALK` 2 the actor walks `pos.x` 690, 692, 694, 695 and the sub-step to 696 is refused (the origin would lie in no section of the body), so it rests inside the cap at `pos.x = 695` with `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` counting every tick on which it presses a key *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the counting rule above; the trap is a strip, not a point: box `[x - 8, x + 8)` straddles the plate's east edge for `pos.x` 689 to 695, where west deepens the overlap (120 to 128 at 689) and refused, so an east input converges to `pos.x = 695` from any start in the strip; from `pos.x` 680 to 688 the box lies wholly inside the plate, west keeps the overlap at 128 and is admitted, and the actor walks back onto the floor; in y the strip spans `pos.y` 240 to 328, the rows for which the box lies wholly inside the plate's rows `[240, 336)`, and at the margins `pos.y` 233 to 239 and 329 to 335 the neighbouring hull-wall rectangle joins `E` and the outcome depends on Layout's neighbour geometry, which the fixture does not fix — D.11 states the full admitted-move set)*. That is a stuck state, and it is not a safe one. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The exposure rule for a footprint-resident exempt actor, stated once (BDY-16, BDY-29, D.11 repeat it).** The first draft added that the trapped actor's "every air, heat and pressure reading ... is the reading of a section it is still in"; that sentence was false and is struck. Body guarantees only that `actor_section` answers a section of the actor's own body (the origin `(695, 282)` lies in plate A). Suit does not read the section: it reads Layout `room_at(section_id, actor_local_px)`, and Layout answers NONE for any point inside a wall footprint (LY-5, LY:905; a `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN` hatch is a bare SOLID `HULL` plate with no room, LY-15), and Suit maps a NONE that is not `IN_POD` to EXPOSED (SE-3, SE:342; the Graph answers the exterior's atmosphere, LSG:206). **Rule (option (c), adopted): an exempt actor whose foot origin lies inside a footprint rectangle of its own body (the cap trap, and residual (i) while it stays inside) is EXPOSED: it takes the exterior's values (vacuum, anoxic, exterior temperature) on a pressurised ship until its origin leaves the footprint or the game restarts from the last autosave.** Options (a) and (b) were examined and rejected. (a) Layout owns the answer for a plate cell and it is NONE; Body cannot write "the adjoining room" over a designed neighbour, so that is an ASK to Layout (Open Question 31) that would supersede this paragraph if adopted. (b) "origin in a section AND `room_at != NONE`" cannot help here: the trapped actor's START origin is already inside the plate, so `room_at` already answers NONE; the one shrinking direction is refused by the same containment and every other direction is refused by the overlap rule, so (b) freezes the actor where it stands, still EXPOSED. **A door-leaf exemption is not exposed:** a closed leaf sits on the door's sill and `room_at` answers the door's `sill_room` there (LY-5), so only wall and hull-plate (cap) footprints read NONE. **How this meets Pillar 1:** the actor is exactly where its feet are, visibly inside the plate, and Suit's own instruments report the exterior band it is standing in (the bands and cues are Suit's); the world does not lie, but the guarantee is **visibility, not safety**, and no sentence of this GDD claims otherwise. Body offers no rescue (a push-out is struck); the primary guard is that the state is unreachable (Assembly's refusal, deferral and the P2 tell window, and BM4's apply-time refusal, BDY-24); recovery belongs to Assembly (a re-weld), to Save/Load (the death-restart) or to the content fix (Open Question 27). This is why **Assembly's refusal (player cut) and deferral plus the P2 tell window (system cut) are the primary guard, a named must-repeat** (BDY-24, 8.3), BM4's apply-time refusal stands behind them (BDY-24 (iii)), and this rule is only the residual net for a restore or a template defect; `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` in the debug overlay makes every such tick visible. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Trapped-actor probe and the restored-while-trapped case (diagnostic only, never a displacement; Body will never rescue).** At each detection event (placement, a transfer, `post_restore`, **and a weld or cut: at BM3 and BM4 the event covers EVERY actor on the bodies the mutator touched, moved or not, because the SOLID rectangle set changed under them — a box left in a SOLID rectangle by a template defect would otherwise first be seen at the next `post_restore`; a cut itself cannot create the D.11 cap trap, because BM4 refuses it first (BDY-24 (iii))**) Body runs, for every actor whose start box gives a non-empty `E`, a bounded read-only probe: for each of the four axis directions it repeats the admitted 1-px sub-step of this paragraph (overlap test plus exit containment) up to `TILE_PX` (48) times from the actor's pose, writing nothing, and asks whether the box reaches a pose that intersects no SOLID rectangle. If none of the four directions does, the actor is **TRAPPED**: `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR` counts, the debug overlay shows it and the pure read `trapped_actors() -> actor_id[]` (ascending; recomputed on every read from current state and never cached, so a stale entry cannot suppress an autosave indefinitely; not persisted, not hashed) lists it. The probe costs at most 4 x 48 box-versus-`E` tests per flagged actor, at those events and on each `trapped_actors()` read (one `solid_in` query per actor to find `E`, at most `MAX_ACTORS` actors per read), never inside `body.integrate` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It exists for one case the restore path creates: **an autosave written while an actor was trapped restores the trap** (positions restore exactly, BDY-31), and the MVP death policy (restart from the last autosave) can then reload into it; the probe makes that visible on the restore, and Body's answer is none beyond that: the remedy is content and authoring validation (Assembly's refusal and deferral keep the state unreachable, BDY-24; Open Question 27) and Save/Load declining to write an autosave while `trapped_actors()` is non-empty, a MUST-REPEAT owned by Save/Load whose acceptance criterion lives in Save/Load's GDD (Open Question 33, 8.3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was an optional ASK)*. The QA gate is `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR` = 0 across every clean-build scenario (AC-BDY-29c). *Decides:* R7, CP-1, PCI:650, LY-11, P2. (auto: D.11 hatch fixture; bounded exit from a partial overlap)
170	
171	**BDY-17 — Actors do not block one another.** In the MVP an actor's foot box collides with Layout rectangles only: two crewmates (and, later, a horror and a crewmate) pass through each other, and two foot boxes overlapping is legal and silent — no diagnostic. Reasons: no player may body-block a crewmate's escape down a corridor in a breach (an ungated friendly-harm vector against the anti-PvP anti-pillar); a doorway jam in the breach rhythm would be chaos from the controls, not from the world (P2); and actor-pair sweeps sit outside the 0.05 ms per actor budget model (PCI:1078). Cites PCI:105 ("no actor pushes another at MVP") and PCI:139. Doors still respect every actor: `leaf_would_overlap` takes every seat's foot box (LY-11, BDY-18), so "a door will not close on any crewmate" still holds. Crowding in a one-tile corridor at four seats is a Vertical Slice question (Open Questions). *Decides:* PCI:105, PCI:139; P2; anti-pillar "no intentional PvP". (auto)
172	
173	**BDY-18 — Door leaves are read in the tick they change; Body supplies the boxes.** Body reads the leaf rectangle set after `layout.doors` (BDY-8). Body publishes `foot_boxes(body_id)` (opaque half-open rectangles, ascending `actor_id`) that Interaction's `validate` gathers for Layout's `leaf_would_overlap(door_ref, area, foot_boxes[])` (IA-24; Layout never reads `body.state`, LY-11). Body does not decide `BLOCKED` or `OBSTRUCTED` (LY-11 notes the Controller spells the reason `BLOCKED` and Interaction `OBSTRUCTED`; neither is Body's) and obeys BDY-16 for the residual door-leaf, restore and template-defect cases *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)*. *Decides:* LY-9, LY-11, IA-24. (auto: PC-18 test 7)
174	
175	**BDY-19 — `odometer` and `blocked`.** `odometer += (|moved_x| + |moved_y|) * ODO_W[move octant]` post-collision (`ODO_W` 256 cardinal, 181 diagonal; 64-bit; PCI:157 amendment 5, PCI:491, PCI:502); walking into a wall adds 0. `blocked` is derived (true on a tick where a non-zero step was requested and the committed `moved` is (0, 0) on both axes), not persisted, not hashed and not replicated, and is **readable by PRESENTATION and DIAGNOSTIC subscribers only; never by a SIM hook** (lint): a SIM hook that read it would make it sim state that must then be persisted and hashed (a schema bump, deliberately). Its SIM-readable sibling is the derived read `moved(actor_id) := pos_curr - pos_prev` (CP-3; States 3.6): it adds no persisted field and is readable by a SIM hook only if that hook is ordered `after: [body.integrate]` (lint). `PC_BLOCKED_TICKS` is the Controller's counter and is cited, not re-registered. *Decides:* R16, PCI:491, PCI:502. (auto: PC-18 test 8; lint)
